mechanism_narrative: The continued rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT should translate into more discretionary trips near business districts, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks as commuting-linked errands and lunch visits recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below the prior four-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below its current level by another 3 points, households are spending more time outside the home, which should raise retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops by at least 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates broader out-of-home activity that spills into shopping and leisure trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or lower over the next 28 days despite both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remaining above their last-week levels.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains depressed relative to WORKPLACES, commuting is being restored by private or local travel rather than public trip chains, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays at least 10 points below WORKPLACES for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains at least 10 points below WORKPLACES for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly increase in PARKS mobility is a short-lag marker of favorable outdoor conditions, and it should pull nearby retail and recreation traffic upward within one week through spillover leisure spending.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week after PARKS posts a week-on-week increase.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RESIDENTIAL keeps falling, households are consolidating trips outside the home, which should produce a modest retail rebound within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM increases while RESIDENTIAL decreases in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening, a sustained narrowing of the gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES means commuting is recovering faster than office attendance losses, and that broadens customer movement into shopping districts over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average even as TRANSIT closes the gap to WORKPLACES over the next month.

mechanism_narrative: The current pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL signals more out-of-home time, but if TRANSIT does not also improve, the effect on retail is weak and RETAIL_REC stays below its prior mean over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the prior four-week mean even though WORKPLACES increases, RESIDENTIAL decreases, and TRANSIT fails to improve.
